name: Virginia

agency.name: Virginia Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ)
agency.division: Air and Renewable Energy Division; regional offices

overview: Virginia DEQ issues air permits under 9VAC5-80 (Permits for Stationary Sources). New sources and projects above the exemption levels in 9VAC5-80-1105 need a minor NSR permit (Article 6), or a state major permit for Title V major facilities that are not PSD. Major sources need PSD (Article 8) in attainment areas or nonattainment NSR (Article 9; Northern Virginia ozone area). Case-by-case MACT is under Article 7. State Operating Permits (Article 5) are elective and usually create synthetic minor limits. Title V permits are under Article 1. General permits cover nonmetallic mineral processing, biomass pilot test facilities, voluntary demand response generators, and emergency generators. There are no local air permitting agencies.

permitTypes.name: Exemptions by size, type, and emission rate
permitTypes.description: Exempt by type or size under 9VAC5-80-1105 B (e.g., fuel-burning equipment below heat input limits, emergency engines below aggregate horsepower limits operating no more than 500 hours per year), or by uncontrolled emission rate under 9VAC5-80-1105 C (new sources) and D (projects); toxic exemption levels are in 9VAC5-80-1105 E. In ozone nonattainment or maintenance areas, fuel-burning thresholds apply in aggregate per fuel type.
permitTypes.quote: Using gaseous fuel with a maximum heat input of less than 50,000,000 Btu per hour.
permitTypes.thresholds: New source exempt rates (uncontrolled, tpy): CO 100, NOx 40, SO2 40, PM 25, PM10 15, PM2.5 10, VOC 25, lead 0.6. Project rates: CO 100, NOx 10, SO2 10, PM 15, PM10 10, PM2.5 6, VOC 10, lead 0.6. Emergency engines: diesel under 1,675 hp (1,125 kW generators), gasoline under 910 hp (611 kW) in aggregate.

permitTypes.name: General Permits
permitTypes.description: Non-metallic mineral processing (9VAC5-510; Forms 510-1/2/3), biomass pilot test facility (Form 520), voluntary demand response generators (Form 530), and emergency generators (Form 540).

permitTypes.name: Minor New Source Review Permit
permitTypes.description: For new sources or projects above the exemption levels at minor facilities. Does not expire. Completeness review 30 days; processing 90 days (180 with public participation). Form 7.
permitTypes.thresholds: Facilities under 100 tpy of any criteria pollutant (restated from DEQ).

permitTypes.name: State Major Permit
permitTypes.description: For Title V major facilities that are not PSD sources. Requires public participation (30-day comment and hearing) and modeling; processing 180 days.
permitTypes.thresholds: More than 100 tpy but less than 250 tpy of a criteria pollutant and not in the 28 listed categories (restated from DEQ).

permitTypes.name: State Operating Permit (SOP)
permitTypes.description: Elective permit, most often used to create synthetic minor limits. Does not expire; at least a 30-day public comment period.

permitTypes.name: Prevention of Significant Deterioration (PSD)
permitTypes.description: New major sources and major modifications in attainment areas. Requires BACT and air quality analysis; review up to 12 months with at least one public hearing.
permitTypes.thresholds: 250 tpy of any regulated pollutant, or 100 tpy for the 28 listed categories, or 100,000 tpy CO2e (restated from DEQ's Air Permits page).

permitTypes.name: Nonattainment NSR
permitTypes.description: Major sources in nonattainment areas; requires LAER and offsets.
permitTypes.thresholds: Northern Virginia Ozone Nonattainment Area (Ozone Transport Region): 100 tpy NOx and/or 50 tpy VOC (restated).

permitTypes.name: Case-by-case MACT (Article 7)
permitTypes.description: Applies to major HAP sources unless a MACT standard applies. Completeness review 45 days; processing normally 180 days.
permitTypes.thresholds: Controlled emissions of 10 tpy of any single HAP or 25 tpy combined (restated from DEQ).

permitTypes.name: Title V Operating Permit
permitTypes.description: Required for facilities above major source thresholds in 9VAC5-80-60 and certain HAP area sources. Form 805; 5-year maximum term; completeness review 60 days; processing 18 months. Title IV acid rain permits also use Form 805.

oilAndGas.summary: DEQ's air permit pages list no oil and gas specific air permit. Natural gas compressor stations and similar sources use the exemption, minor NSR, SOP, and Title V framework above.

notes: Exemption thresholds restated from the 9VAC5-80-1105 text (one heat input phrase quoted verbatim). Article 8 start section is cited inconsistently in the regulation definitions (9VAC5-80-1605 vs -1700).
